compatibility_badge: PCB Layout Change Required (Pinout or Package Mismatch)

pin_diff.note: CRITICAL OUTPUT STAGE DIFFERENCE: OPA333AIDBVR is opamp (push-pull) vs TLV3201AIDBVR comparator (push-pull); a comparator is an uncompensated open-loop switching device (no internal Miller/dominant-pole compensation) and will oscillate or latch in a linear negative-feedback op-amp circuit, while an op-amp used as a comparator suffers slow saturation/overdrive recovery and propagation delay far worse than its slew rate implies; both output stages are push-pull (no pull-up resistor required), so the incompatibility is loop compensation, input clamp behavior, and switching dynamics rather than pull-up drive.
Functionally identical VEE pin (V- vs GND).
Functionally identical IN_POS pin (+IN vs IN+).
Functionally identical IN_NEG pin (-IN vs IN-).
Functionally identical VCC pin (V+ vs VCC).

parameter_matrix.note: Op-amps (internally compensated for linear feedback) and comparators (uncompensated open-loop switching) are NOT drop-in interchangeable.
Single SOT-23-5 op-amps vary in pin ordering across vendors; verify Pin 1–5.
A part wins only if its recommended Vs range strictly encompasses the counterpart on both ends.
Exceeding Vs,abs causes immediate gate-oxide or junction breakdown.
Closed-loop -3 dB bandwidth scales as f_-3dB = GBWP / Acl.
Controls large-signal full-power bandwidth SR / (2π·Vpeak) or comparator switching speed.
Lower Vos minimizes DC error in current-shunt and sensor bridge amplifiers.
CMOS/JFET pA-class inputs avoid offset voltage drops across high-impedance (>100 kΩ) sensors.
Multiply by channel count for total IC standby current draw.
RRIO prevents clipping on low-voltage 3.3 V single-supply ADC buffers.
Winner requires superiority on both CMRR (higher) and input voltage noise (lower); mixed tradeoffs stay CONTEXT.
Important when driving heavy resistive loads or high supply rails.

swap_risks: CRITICAL OP-AMP VS COMPARATOR TRAP: OPA333AIDBVR is a opamp with push-pull output while TLV3201AIDBVR is a comparator with push-pull output. Even with identical pinouts, a comparator is an uncompensated switching device: dropping it into a linear negative-feedback op-amp circuit (buffer, gain stage, filter) causes oscillation or latch-up, and an op-amp used as a comparator suffers slow overdrive/saturation recovery. Both outputs are push-pull (no external pull-up required) — the incompatibility is loop compensation and switching behavior, not pull-up drive.

CAUTION PRECISION OFFSET SHIFT: Maximum Vos differs by 300x (OPA333AIDBVR: 0.01 mV p.7 vs TLV3201AIDBVR: 3 mV p.5); high-gain DC sensor stages may lose accuracy or require zero-drift chopper filtering.

HIGH INPUT BIAS CURRENT SHIFT: Typical Ib differs by 70x (OPA333AIDBVR: 70 pA p.7 vs TLV3201AIDBVR: 1 pA p.5); high-impedance sensor dividers (>100 kΩ) suffer severe Ib·R DC offset error when swapping from CMOS/JFET to bipolar inputs.

CAUTION QUIESCENT CURRENT SHIFT: Supply current per channel differs by 2.4x (OPA333AIDBVR: 17 µA/ch p.7 vs TLV3201AIDBVR: 40 µA/ch p.5); verify battery budget and total power dissipation across all channels.
HIGH MINIMUM SUPPLY FLOOR: TLV3201AIDBVR requires Vs,min >= 2.7 V (p.4) vs 1.8 V on the counterpart; confirm low-battery / brown-out operation still clears the higher floor.
engineering_verdict: OPA333AIDBVR (Texas Instruments, SOT-23-5) and TLV3201AIDBVR (Texas Instruments, SOT-23-5) are NOT drop-in interchangeable (Level 3 PCB Layout / Circuit Change Required) due to device kind mismatch (opamp/push-pull vs comparator/push-pull) — circuit redesign required. Specific pin conflicts: Pin 1 (OUT vs OUT). Signal-chain deltas: opamp (push-pull) vs comparator (push-pull), supply ceiling 5.5 V (p.5) vs 5.5 V (p.4), Vos 0.01 mV (p.7) vs 3 mV (p.5), Ib 70x gap (70 vs 1 pA). Primary bench gotchas to watch: OPA333AIDBVR "Weak ±5 mA Output Drive and 350 kHz / 0.16 V/µs Speed Limit vs Pin-Identical TLV9001/TLV9061" (p.7) and TLV3201AIDBVR "Push-Pull Output — Do NOT Wired-AND or Pull Up to a Different Logic Rail" (p.5). BOM decision: Choose OPA333AIDBVR when the circuit is a linear closed-loop amplifier, buffer, or active filter or DC precision demands <= 0.01 mV max Vos; choose TLV3201AIDBVR when the circuit is an open-loop threshold/window comparator (push-pull output) or high-impedance sensors require pA-class input bias (1 pA). Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.3) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
